subject: climbing perch
title: A Fish Walks Between Ponds for Days, and It Chokes Whatever Eats It

scenes.text: This fish kills the bird that swallows it.
The climbing perch of Asia. It breathes air and survives up to six days out of water.
It drags itself from pond to pond on its gill plates and can hibernate in mud for six months.
Swallow one, and it flares its spiny gill covers and swells. The predator chokes, or starves with it lodged in its throat.
It has already walked onto two Australian islands, six kilometres from New Guinea.
So it isn't lunch. It's a trap with fins.

description:
The climbing perch walks overland between waterholes, survives up to six days out of water, and kills the predators that swallow it.
The fish breathes air with a special organ, drags itself across land using its gill plates, and can wait out a dry season buried in mud for up to six months. When a bird or larger fish swallows it, it flares its spiny gill covers and inflates its body, so the predator chokes or starves. It has reached the Australian islands of Boigu and Saibai, four to six kilometres from Papua New Guinea, and James Cook University researchers warn it could spread to the mainland.
What would you do if a fish walked past you on dry land?
first_comment: It was first recorded on the islands in 2005 and has been creeping south ever since. Which invasive animal worries you most?
